study_type_evidence.quote: Onc72 and both prodrugs were administered as single SC dose of 4.34 µmol kg-1 bodyweight to female CD-1 mice (20-29 g, 12-16 weeks old...)
An aqueous solution of a PEGylated prodrug (105 µmol L-1, 15 µL) was mixed with mouse serum (35 µL)
Human blood was collected in EDTA tubes, stored at room temperature (RT) for 60 min, centrifuged (5 min, 1000 x g, 4 degrees C)
Onc72 and both prodrugs were dissolved (final concentration of 31.5 µmol L-1) in E. coli BW25113 lysate (0.5 g L-1 protein)
Human hepatoma (HepG2) and human embryonic kidney cells (HEK293) were cultured in DMEM/Ham's F12 medium containing fetal bovine serum

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female CD-1 mice, 20-29 g, 12-16 weeks old (Charles River Laboratories, Senneville, QC, Canada)
in_vivo_species.quote: administered as single SC dose of 4.34 µmol kg-1 bodyweight to female CD-1 mice (20-29 g, 12-16 weeks old, Charles River Laboratories...)

ex_vivo_detail: Animal: Onc72 release and prodrug degradation measured in normal mouse serum (Invitrogen/Thermo Fisher) at 31.5 µmol/L, 37 degrees C, over 0-24 h; mouse serum (25% v/v) also added to bacterial growth, MIC and CFU assays. Human: hemolytic-activity assay used washed erythrocytes from human blood collected in EDTA tubes (Institutional Review Board of Leipzig University AZ 313/14-ek).
in_vitro_detail: E. coli BW25113 cell lysate (0.5 g/L protein) stability assay; broth microdilution MIC and growth-kinetics/viable-count assays in 19% MHB2 medium; cytotoxicity on human HepG2 and HEK293 cell lines (MTT); Onc72 release by purified human alpha-thrombin in Tris-buffered saline; competitive ELISA validation.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figure 5 (adhm202202368-fig-0005), panels a-f; also Figure 1 for ex vivo serum release
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Concentration profiles obtained for plasma samples collected from CD-1 mice after subcutaneous injection of Onc72 a,b), 5k-prodrug c,d), and 20k-prodrug e,f)
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 5 plots plasma concentration versus time (5 min to 24 h) after a single SC dose in CD-1 mice, quantified by cELISA (panels a, c, e) and by mass spectrometry for released Onc72 (panels b, d, f). Figure 1 additionally plots ex vivo recovery/release (normalized peak areas, i.e. %-remaining) versus time for both prodrugs incubated in mouse serum. Figure S11 (Supporting Information, referenced in body) shows urine concentrations over time.

bioanalytical_method: Competitive ELISA (cELISA) using protein-G-captured anti-Onc72 monoclonal antibody 4H6 with carboxyfluorescein-Onc72 reporter (fluorescence, lambda-exc 485 nm / lambda-em 535 nm) for total Onc72; plus LC-MS (ACQUITY UPLC M-Class coupled to ESI-QTOF Synapt G2-Si, scheduled multiple reaction monitoring) with 13C,15N-labeled Onc72 internal standard for free Onc72 and metabolites; RP-HPLC/ESI-IT-MS for serum and lysate release experiments; HDMSE for urine metabolite identification
bioanalytical_quote: the plasma concentrations of Onc72 and prodrugs were determined using reversed-phase liquid chromatography coupled online to mass spectrometry (RPLC-MS) and a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (cELISA).
notes: Elimination half-lives are for total Onc72-immunoreactive material (prodrug + released Onc72 + epitope-containing metabolites) measured by cELISA; Table 1 gives t1/2 43, 66 and 324 min for Onc72, 5k-prodrug and 20k-prodrug respectively, while the body text describes the 20k-prodrug value as '~5.5 h'. The ex vivo mouse-serum release half-lives (8 h for 5k-prodrug, 14 h for 20k-prodrug) come from Figure 1 and are release, not elimination, half-lives. Additional Table 1 parameters: V 47.3 / 115.3 / 171.8 mL, AUC0-inf 5.5 / 12.7 / 139 µg x h/mL, CL 0.76 / 1.22 / 0.35 mL min-1, MRT 53 / 111 / 524 min. The body states Onc72 has a reported mouse-serum half-life of ~3 h and an intraperitoneal elimination t1/2 of ~14 min, but both are explicitly attributed to earlier publications and were therefore not extracted. Mice were grouped by blood-sampling timepoint (groups 1-3) rather than by a fixed n per arm. LOD/LOQ: 4.5 and 9 µg L-1 for Onc72; cELISA urine LOQ 46 µg L-1. Lower-detail agents also present in the body but not separately listed: human alpha-thrombin (enzymatic release reagent), Cf-Onc72 reporter, mAb 4H6, recombinant protein G, casein.
